assertions.name: su_n_quantum_dimension_matches_minus_bracket_N
assertions.source: Route A: δ = (v⁻¹−v)/z with v = q₀^{N/2}, z = √q₀−1/√q₀ — the point the engine evaluates at. Route B: −[N]_s = −(s^N−s^{−N})/(s−s^{−1}) at s = √q₀ — the defining rep's quantum dimension. Expected = the channel list rebuilt from range(2, N_max+1), so raising N_max tightens this. Guards the 2026-06-04 v-exponent fix (audit §2e).

assertions.name: figure_eight_amphichiral_in_every_su_n_channel
assertions.source: Route A: P(σ₁σ₂⁻¹σ₁σ₂⁻¹; SU(N), q₀). Route B: P of the mirror word σ₁⁻¹σ₂σ₁⁻¹σ₂. 4₁ is amphichiral, so agreement is a known property, not a restatement. Worst gap this run: 1.776e-15.

assertions.name: borromean_mirror_pair_has_zero_channel_split
assertions.source: Route A: P((σ₁σ₂⁻¹)³; SU(N), q₀). Route B: P((σ₁⁻¹σ₂)³) — its mirror. Both close to the Borromean rings, which is amphichiral, so this engine returns no p/n split in ANY channel: the ratio column is 1.0 throughout and the Q_β back-solve has no input. Recorded so a later engine that does split the pair flips this rather than passing silently.

description: First multi-channel HOMFLYPT evaluation of the mass tower at substrate q₀. Computes P(β̂; SU(N), q₀) for N=2..6 across proton, neutron, figure-eight, and trefoil braids. Records per-N proton/neutron ratios, mirror differences (CPT structure), and Q_β predictor candidates. Per rem:archimedean-image-table row 5: this is the first data from the SU(N>2) channels.
caveats: The p/n mirror difference is identically zero at every N, so the 'multi-channel mass-split data' and the |ΔP| Q_β back-solve in the docstring produce nothing at all — the back-solve block prints no rows. Separately, the absolute normalisation is confirmed broken in this run: the 2-strand trefoil σ₁³ comes out 14%–44% away from Lickorish's P(3₁⁺; v, z) = 2v² − v⁴ + v²z² at the same (v, z), so no absolute value here is assertable and only δ and mirror pairs are.
